relationships.subject: MIA-690
relationships.evidence_quote: The GHRH antagonist MIA-690 (1 and 5 μM) and GHRH agonist MR-409 (1 and 5 μM) were shown to decrease LPS-induced PGE2 and 8-iso-PGF2α levels, in a dose-dependent manner

relationships.subject: MR-409
relationships.evidence_quote: DSS treatment significantly stimulated both PGE2 and 8-iso-PGF2α levels, and both MIA-690 (5 µg) and MR-409 (5 µg) reduced these effects

relationships.subject: MIA-690
relationships.evidence_quote: The GHRH antagonist MIA-690 (1 and 5 μM) decreased inflammatory markers after LPS treatment in a dose-dependent manner

relationships.subject: MIA-690
relationships.evidence_quote: MIA-690 (5 µg) decreased TNF-α, IL-6 and iNOS gene expression

relationships.subject: MIA-690
relationships.evidence_quote: ELISA results showed a significant reduction in circulating levels of IGF-1 in MIA-690 (5 μg) treated mice, but not in MR-409 (5 μg) treated mice

key_findings: GHRH antagonist MIA-690 and agonist MR-409 reduce LPS-induced PGE2, COX-2, NF-kB, iNOS ex vivo and attenuate DSS colitis; MIA-690 is more effective and lowers serum IGF-1.
Both analogs reduce hot-plate and formalin nociceptive responses.
